domain_assessments.domain: Terminal oxidation and experimental taxon scope
domain_assessments.assessment: TynA terminal assignment is native hypothetical EV-AS-NAS, not experimentally established aminoacetone catalysis in E. coli. The 1968 unnamed sewage isolate was described as closely related to Arthrobacter globiformis, not a resolved modern strain accession. Washed-cell methylglyoxal/O2 data and the proposed peroxide/catalase equation do not establish measured H2O2 or an identified oxidase. E. coli W1485/SBD76 aminoacetone non-growth/non-consumption and Serratia Sr41 unresolved further metabolism remain assay/strain bounded. Cytoplasmic Tdh and periplasmic TynA do not establish an intervening aminoacetone transport mechanism.

Entire eight-page publisher PDF inspected. MG1655-derived orf382 was expressed as N-terminal six-His protein in BL21(DE3); the exact construct sequence was not supplied. Original AAB18566.1 is 382 aa; current P37686 is 383 aa with C-terminal differences independently compared. NADH340nm supports oxidation activity without directly measured intermediate/product or whole-route reconstruction. Metal assay/EDTA/CD evidence and Keio-versus-paper glycine phenotype conflict retain their stated limits. Table2 locator is erroneous.

SstT sodium/threonine and TdcC proton/threonine directions and annotations, LIV-I ATP-dependent activity without invented complete stoichiometry, and three opaque pathway interfaces are supported. LIV transcription and transport responses remain condition dependent; ilvIH DNA-binding assays are not promoted to tdh/liv promoter binding. FeaR reporter effects and C-terminal six-His DNA-binding domain are distinct from full-length ligand-binding. NsrR native annotation, altered start-codon expression, and species/strain qualifications remain explicit; no supported tynA metal occupancy or direct allosteric flux claim is invented.

Author iModulonDB assessment and exact identifiers were inspected; target audit finds no iModulon membership promoted to catalysis or causal route proof. Reviewer did not independently replay all 32 author adapter bodies. Search absence is not negative biological evidence or source exhaustion.

84 unique named IDs, 72 participants, nine reaction/activity/interface nodes, two taxa, 111 unique edges, 83 references and local endpoint/reference closure pass. findings.title: L-serine competition is assigned to alanine
findings.rule: A near miss is not a match; verify exact metabolite identity and narrow experimental scope.
findings.observation: The edge subject CHEBI:16449 is alanine, while its assertion and original experiment concern excess L-serine. Table 1 reports normalized uptake 0.23 with L-serine, 0.81 with L-alanine, and 0.20 in the tdc-deleted control; the source text says alanine did not significantly affect uptake. Thus the graph asserts the wrong chemical interaction despite correct narrative.
findings.source_locator: Original J Bacteriol 172 (1990), p4291, Table 1 and Characterization of the transport system; TH16(pEC61), anaerobic induction, 0.5 mM competitor (50-fold).
findings.remedy: Replace the erroneous subject and corresponding participant with authority-backed CHEBI:17115 L-serine. CHEBI:33384 may be used only with explicit source-neutral-to-zwitterion normalization. Remove the alanine inhibition assertion; retain whole-cell competition rather than allosteric inhibition, and preserve all other graph scope.
acceptance: Re-read the original assay table and exact ChEBI definition for the selected L-serine endpoint.
Add a source-backed negative control which restores CHEBI:16449 and must fail independently of narrative labels.
Refresh source/edge/identity ledgers, authority artifacts, render and KGX after correction; preserve all 111 edges unless a separately supported correction is made.

findings.title: Optional explicit disclosure of historical TdcC sequence provenance
findings.rule: Non-blocking experimental-material provenance clarification; do not invent a variant from a historical sequence discrepancy.
findings.observation: The original p4292 Discussion/Fig5 describes 431 residues; current P0AAD8 is 443 residues and annotates historical sequence conflicts at 70 and 431–443. The draft makes no explicit full-sequence/material-equivalence assertion and already bounds these edges to whole-cell competition/energetic assays. This is not evidence that the assayed transporter was an engineered truncation or a distinct physical variant.
findings.remedy: A concise shared note may disclose the historical 431-aa report versus the current 443-aa reference and that the complete assayed sequence is not established. Keep MC4100/TH16(pEC61) assay scope and do not conflate separate PhoA/LacZ topology fusions with the transport preparation. Do not add an invented variant node.
acceptance: Any added sequence/material note states the uncertainty rather than equating a reporting discrepancy with a proven assayed variant.
Retain the existing cell-assay and no-purified-binding qualifiers.
